newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan exporters fall, importers rise on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: Japan exporters fall, importers rise on strong yen.

text.p: Shares in Japanese exporters fell on Monday morning while shares in importers and domestic-demand related stocks, which benefit from a stronger yen, rose on the yen's early-morning rally against the dollar, brokers said.

As of 0033 GMT, shares in Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd had slipped 60 yen to 2,160 with 1.55 million shares traded. It was the third most actively traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Sony Corp slumped 210 yen to 9,310. Toyota Motor Corp fell 130 yen to 3,690. Honda Motor Co Ltd shed 140 yen to trade at 3,890.

"Blue chip exporters are being sold due to the strengthening of the yen, but rather than the selling itself, investors are interested in seeing how far the shares will fall," said Shigeru Okamoto at Kankaku Securities.
"In the past, bottom-fishing moves supported Sony at a fairly early point."
Pulp/paper, oil and mining sector shares were mostly higher.
Oji Paper Co Ltd jumped 27 yen to 727, with trade totalling 1.57 million shares, making it the fourth most heavily traded issue. Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd climbed 28 yen to 648.
Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd rose 29 yen to 547 and Showa Shell Sekiyu KK advanced 34 yen to 995.
Arabian Oil Co Ltd added 130 yen to stand at 3,860 and Kanto Natural Gas Development Co Ltd was up nine yen at 669.

Market sources said that the main focus was not on the stronger yen's impact on the Nikkei average itself, but what sort of shares will be bought instead of the blue chips that helped boost the Nikkei by over six percent in the first month of the new business year alone.
"Dealers are actively trading shares which benefit from a stronger yen this morning," a dealer at a second-tier brokerage said.
In pre-market hours, the yen leapt as high as 117.60 yen to the dollar at one point in early Tokyo trade, compared with 123.11/21 yen on Friday in late afternoon Tokyo.

"How the Nikkei average does this week, or whether exporters come back to life or not depends on how far the yen strengthens," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager, said. "Exporters have their yen/dollar rates set at around 115 yen, so as long as it does not go past that level, there should not be too much cause for alarm."
